derivedGeography.data: OpenFreeMap · © OpenMapTiles · © OpenStreetMap contributors. CMAB V7 by Yecheng Zhang, Huimin Zhao and Ying Long (CC BY 4.0). Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2025.
derivedGeography.processing: city-layout.bin merges mapped building parts and imagery-derived roof outlines with estimated infill frontages inside mapped residential and commercial areas. The local mapped networks and hydrography are in urban-streets.json and inland-water.json. The street, water and building database extracts derived from OpenStreetMap are available under ODbL 1.0. See the geographic credits for individual sources, attribution and modifications.
derivedGeography.lakeBanks: Riparian canopy positions combine mapped woodland and parkland, Sentinel-2 optical vegetation and the new water, road and roof masks. Individual trees are approximate.
derivedGeography.oldTown: The street alignments, foreshore, park, hotel, customs building, terminal, pontoons and gangways in src/old-town-plan.json derive from © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. Shop lots, facade details and landscaping are reconstructed. tools/prepare-old-town.py reproduces this extract.
derivedGeography.railway: src/railway-plan.json derives the station outline, squares, ancillary buildings, five platform extents and the nine track alignments from © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. Coordinates are transformed to local metres, simplified, and adjusted locally to clear platform edges. Heights and train movements are reconstructed for the game.

gaoqiRailway.data: src/gaoqi-railway-plan.json derives the Gaoqi yards, sections of the Yingtan–Xiamen and Dongdu Port railways, platform outlines and selected buildings from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0, API extract 2026-11-25). tools/prepare-gaoqi-railway.py extracts the features into the game's metre grid.
gaoqiRailway.imagery: Vantor imagery acquired 2025-03-20, served through Esri World Imagery, was consulted for the Gaoqi railway yards, station-house roofs, forecourt and approach roads. The imagery is not bundled in the game.
gaoqiRailway.reconstruction: Building heights, railway elevations, catenary, finishes and freight car placement are reconstructed. The red roof lettering is documented in archival photographs. Its present condition is unverified, so the current scene identifies the station in the HUD.

derivedGeography.wucun: src/wucun-plan.json and wucun-ground.webp derive carriageways, the BRT alignment, parcels and selected footprints from © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. tools/prepare-wucun.py generates the extract and ground artwork. Architectural heights, façades, pedestrian bridges, road markings, lighting and moving vehicles are reconstructed for the game.
derivedGeography.northernCrossings: src/north-crossings-plan.json contains centerlines and approach ramps derived from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0, API extract 2026-11-24). The two directional ways are paired into an alignment, simplified and projected at runtime onto the game's metre grid. Esri World Imagery was consulted as a visual comparison for shoreline contacts and retaining embankments.

brt.data: src/brt-plan.json uses route ways and boarding areas from © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, extracted 2026-11-24. tools/prepare-brt.py reproduces the extract in local metres.
brt.reconstruction: The box girders, vase-shaped piers, station roofs and interchange levels follow the design report and visual references. Bearing placement, stair clearances, electric bus details, elevation profiles, island branch turnarounds and headways are reconstructed for the game.

art: Landmarks, airport structures, vessels, street furniture, roof finishes, facades and vegetation are rendered for this game. Heights with no source record are estimated. Individual roof shapes and illuminated windows are artistic reconstructions.
night: Night emission follows the merged building footprints and mapped road network. The lighting of individual buildings, bridges, windows and the moon is an artistic reconstruction.

island.terrain: Gulangyu uses local z14 Mapzen Terrarium samples on a 10 m mesh. Xiamen Island uses a 25 m mesh derived from Copernicus GLO-30. The outlying terrain uses the original 50 m mesh.
island.layout: The Gulangyu shoreline in /geo/islands.json and the paths, reef, heritage footprints and ferry structures in src/gulangyu-plan.json derive from © OpenStreetMap contributors (API extract 2026-11-24). tools/prepare-gulangyu-sites.py extracts the mapped ways and projects them into local metres. The north berth was updated from the ferry operator's post-reconstruction photographs and filing.
island.landscape: gulangyu-ground.webp and gulangyu-cover.bin use the bundled OpenFreeMap/OpenMapTiles land-cover, street and building data and Copernicus Sentinel optical imagery credited above. Individual trees, coastal rocks, roof profiles, arcades, pavement and lighting are artistic reconstructions.

landmarkReferences.site: 厦门高崎国际机场
landmarkReferences.pavementGeometry: tools/prepare-airport-pavement.py merges runway, drawn apron and taxiway footprints into disjoint surfaces. Terminal access ramps follow the mapped public streets.
landmarkReferences.landsideReconstruction: The T3 garden and T4 surface parking and open lawn follow aerial imagery and public descriptions. Terrace slopes, marked bays and planted islands are drawn at scene scale.
landmarkReferences.reconstruction: Airfield surfaces and terminal footprints were traced against Esri World Imagery, with selected taxiway centre lines, the T4 footprint and T4 gate references checked against © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0). The game models roof and façade details, the tower, apron equipment, parked aircraft and lighting.

landmarkReferences.site: 海沧大桥
翔安大桥

inscription.reconstruction: The original brush outlines and the red inscription on the 9 by 3 metre board follow the unveiling and the selection gallery. The location between the main deck and a ramp at the Xiang'an end is estimated from the aerial photograph. The column and engraving depths are estimated.

landmarkReferences.reconstruction: The eight-lane single steel box girder, three fairway areas and the middle unit's 90/90/150/150/90/90 m sequence follow the public records. Bridge elevations, the exact planting of piers, outer fairway spans, junction levels and scene lighting are estimated.

landmarkReferences.site: 集美大桥

inscription.reconstruction: The map marks this scene as a reconstruction of the 2008 opening plaque. The red title, signature and fluted pedestal follow archival photographs. Opening coverage records markers at both ends. The north-bank position and dimensions are estimates, and the present condition of the north-bank plaque is unverified. The island-side plaque was damaged in 2016.

landmarkReferences.reconstruction: The mapped curve and the central two BRT lanes between three highway lanes in each direction follow the owner and environmental report. The Lehai Road widening and the North Airport approach are simplified. Pier intervals, elevations and lamp positions are estimated from photographs and the game terrain.

landmarkReferences.site: 厦门大桥

inscription.reconstruction: The gilded raised brush lettering and pink granite follow the Gaoqi bridgehead park photographs. The exact position in the park, proportions and relief depth are estimated.

landmarkReferences.reconstruction: The model uses paired rectangular piers for the 46 divisions of the 45 m continuous box girder, a central joint, and the current six-lane deck. The start station of the span grid, elevations, ramp transitions and lighting are estimated.

landmarkReferences.site: 高集海堤（厦门海堤高崎至集美段）

inscription.reconstruction: The gaoji brush outlines in src/north-inscription-strokes.json adapt 大禾花’s photo under CC BY-SA 4.0 through perspective correction and vector tracing. The front title and signature are modeled at the mapped Gaoqi memorial. The orientation, stair and stone profiles are estimated from photographs.

landmarkReferences.reconstruction: The Gaoqi and Jimei openings are modeled at 850 m and 210 m along the causeway. The remaining stone-faced embankment, two road lanes, cycling path and separate Metro Line 1 viaduct follow the mapped arrangement. Exact gap edges, slopes, deck levels, rail vehicles and lamps are estimated.

landmarkReferences.site: 演武大桥与观景平台
landmarkReferences.reconstruction: OpenStreetMap geometry was extracted on 2026-11-25 and checked against Esri World Imagery, whose local capture date was unverified. The April 2017 aerial publication records the original crescent geometry. The November 2022 report records the completed Starlight Coast and twelve No. 2 entrance portals. August 2026 coverage confirms the three entrances and Starlight Coast's continued use. The image capture dates in the August coverage are unstated. The October 2026 maintenance report and June repair approval do not establish completed visible changes to the bridge. The mesh includes the 26 m through deck, 1.6 m fish-belly beam profile, oval piers, Chenggong and Yanwu interchange ramps, the Baicheng landings, and the three lookout accesses. Grades, pier locations and spacing, rail profiles, local paving, the placement and dimensions of the portals, night lighting, and minor landside paths are estimated.

summitPhotos: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:日光岩顶峰和山下的鼓浪屿与思明区_7.jpg
landmarkReferences.surfaceDetail: Rock Boulder Dry by Dimitrios Savva and Rico Cilliers, Poly Haven (CC0). The luminance and OpenGL normal XY channels are packed locally and projected onto the modeled rocks. https://polyhaven.com/a/rock_boulder_dry
